c.tagline: Fujian's island city of colonial Gulangyu, sea breezes, and oolong tea.

taxi.fareNote: Metered fares start around ¥10; most locals hail rides or pay via Didi and mobile QR (Alipay/WeChat), and some drivers may not accept foreign cards or make change for large notes.

emergency.note: 110 for police, 120 for ambulance/medical, and 119 for fire. English-speaking operators may be limited; hotel staff can help translate.

avoid.reason: Watch for pickpockets and 'tea ceremony' overcharging scams in crowded spots like Zhongshan Road and the Gulangyu ferry queues.

hood_desc: The walkable old-town core around Zhongshan Road pedestrian street, the Gulangyu ferry piers, Shapowei fishing harbor, and Bailuzhou; the best base for first-timers who want sights, seafood, and the waterfront all within reach.

Gulangyu, the UNESCO-listed car-free island of colonial villas, the piano museum, and winding leafy lanes; an atmospheric, romantic stay for those who don't mind carrying luggage on foot and want the island to themselves after the day-trippers leave.
A laid-back seaside strip beside Xiamen University and the ring-road beaches, packed with hostels, cafes, murals, and cheap eats; suits students, backpackers, and beach-goers.
A modern commercial district around SM City Plaza and Jiahe Road with easy metro, BRT, and ferry connections; good for shoppers, business travelers, and anyone who values convenient transit.

A quieter mainland district across the bridge known for the Jimei School Village, Chen Jiageng's heritage architecture, and Jimei University; cheaper and more local, good for travelers wanting everyday Fujian life and heritage.

water.note: Stick to bottled or boiled water; avoid tap water and ice made from it.

transit.hours: The metro runs roughly 6:00 AM to 11:00 PM, with BRT and main bus lines on similar hours and only limited night buses. Gulangyu ferries run day and night on a reduced overnight schedule.
transit.note: Xiamen has a growing metro network, an elevated BRT (Bus Rapid Transit) busway, extensive city buses, and frequent passenger ferries to Gulangyu Island.
transit.pay: Pay with the Xiamen e-Tong transit card, a QR code through Alipay/WeChat, or contactless; single metro rides run about ¥2-¥5 and buses ¥1-¥2. Foreign visitors can link an international card to Alipay or WeChat to pay by QR.

bus: Intercity coaches to Quanzhou, Zhangzhou, and Fuzhou

car.idp: Not recognized (a Chinese driving license is required)

ferry: Ferries to Gulangyu Island (from Lundu and Dongdu terminals)
train: Xiamen Railway Station and Xiamen North Railway Station (high-speed rail to Fuzhou, Shenzhen, and Shanghai)

transit.m: Airport bus / BRT connection to city center (~30-40 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary or expected in China; a service charge may be added at high-end hotels and restaurants.
